providers.name: OpenAI API
notes: This is the OpenAI developer platform API (api.openai.com/v1), which is separate from the ChatGPT product. All endpoints share the host https://api.openai.com and authenticate with a secret API key sent as Authorization: Bearer <OPENAI_API_KEY>; optional OpenAI-Organization / OpenAI-Project headers select the organization and project.
API keys are secrets: call the API from a server, never from browser or mobile client code.

Rate limits are per organization/project and per model (RPM, RPD, TPM, TPD, IPM); paid usage tiers are Build, Launch and Grow. 429 responses should be retried after Retry-After or with exponential backoff and jitter.

The Responses API (POST /v1/responses) is recommended for new projects; Chat Completions remains supported. In Responses, generated text is inside output[] message items (content[] parts of type output_text). The output_text property shown in SDK examples is an SDK convenience, not a documented REST field.

Structured Outputs: Responses uses text.format {type: json_schema, name, schema, strict}; Chat Completions uses response_format {type: json_schema, json_schema: {...}}. json_object (JSON mode) produces JSON but does not ensure schema adherence.

Data controls: API data is not used for training unless the customer opts in. Responses are stored for 30 days by default (store defaults to true). Files uploaded to /v1/files are kept until deleted and /v1/files is not Zero Data Retention eligible.
The Assistants API was sunset on August 26, 2026 and is included only as a flagged deprecated distractor.

Model choice: scenarios assess model parameters by documented capability (model pages list modalities and features such as image input or Structured Outputs), not by ranking or price. Model IDs change often; the models page was checked 2026-10-17.
The full Responses reference pages are very long; fields that could not be read in full (for example the complete list of output item types) are modeled partially and noted in research/openai.md.

endpoints.title: Create a model response
endpoints.description: Creates a model response from text, image or file inputs and returns generated text or JSON. Recommended for new projects (Chat Completions remains supported). The response object's output array holds message items whose content parts contain the generated text; reasoning or tool-call items may appear before the message. Responses are stored for 30 days by default (store defaults to true).

parameters.name: model
parameters.description: Model ID used to generate the response, like gpt-6-astra. The reference marks it optional (a saved prompt can supply one), but documented example requests always set it. Choose a model whose model page lists the capabilities the request needs (for example image input or Structured Outputs); the model pages at developers.openai.com/api/docs/models list modalities and features.

parameters.name: input
parameters.description: Text, image, or file inputs to the model. Either a plain string, or an array of input items. A message item has role (user, assistant, system, developer) and content: a string or an array of content parts. Content parts: {type: input_text, text}; {type: input_image, image_url (a fully qualified URL or a base64 data URL) or file_id (from the Files API), detail: low|high|auto|original (default auto)}; {type: input_file, file_id, file_url, or file_data (base64 data URL, e.g. data:application/pdf;base64,...), filename}. Each file must be under 50 MB and all files in one request together under 50 MB. Audio is not accepted as input_file.

parameters.name: instructions
parameters.description: A system (or developer) message inserted into the model's context. Takes priority over the prompt in input. Applies only to this request: it is not carried over when previous_response_id is used.

parameters.name: text
parameters.description: Configuration for the text output. text.format is one of: {type: text} (default, plain text); {type: json_schema, name, schema, strict, description} (Structured Outputs: with strict true the output follows the supplied JSON Schema; documented examples set additionalProperties false and list every property in required); {type: json_object} (older JSON mode: valid JSON, but does not ensure schema adherence). Replaces Chat Completions' response_format. Structured Outputs requires a model whose page lists Structured Outputs support.

parameters.name: max_output_tokens
parameters.description: Upper bound on generated tokens, including visible output and reasoning tokens. If reached, status is incomplete with incomplete_details.reason max_output_tokens, possibly before any visible text.

parameters.name: temperature
parameters.description: Sampling temperature between 0 and 2. Alter this or top_p, not both.

parameters.name: store
parameters.description: Whether to store the generated model response for later retrieval via API. Defaults to true; stored Response objects are kept for 30 days by default.

parameters.name: previous_response_id
parameters.description: The ID of a previous response, to continue a multi-turn conversation with OpenAI managing the earlier context. Cannot be used together with conversation.

parameters.name: conversation
parameters.description: ID of a conversation (Conversations API) this response belongs to. Cannot be used together with previous_response_id.

parameters.name: tools
parameters.description: Tools the model may call: built-in tools such as {type: file_search, vector_store_ids: [...]} (vector_store_ids required) or {type: web_search}, MCP tools, or your own function tools.

parameters.name: metadata
parameters.description: Up to 16 key-value pairs (keys up to 64 characters, values up to 512).

parameterRules.description: previous_response_id cannot be used together with conversation.

authentication.description: Send a secret API key (or a short-lived workload identity federation access token) as a Bearer token. The key is a secret: load it on a server from an environment variable or key management service and never put it in browser or mobile client code. If you belong to several organizations or use a legacy user key, the optional OpenAI-Organization and OpenAI-Project headers choose which organization and project the request uses.

rateLimits.description: Rate limits are set per organization and project (not per user) and vary by model. endpoints.title: Create chat completion
endpoints.description: Generates a model reply to a list of messages. Still supported, though the Responses API is recommended for new projects. The generated text is in choices[].message.content. User message content parts can be text, image_url {url, detail}, input_audio {data (base64), format: wav or mp3}, or file {file_id or file_data, filename}; for files Chat Completions supports only PDF.

parameters.name: model
parameters.description: Model ID used to generate the response. Choose a model whose model page lists the capabilities the request needs (for example image input or Structured Outputs); the model pages at developers.openai.com/api/docs/models list modalities and features.

parameters.name: messages
parameters.description: The conversation so far. Each message has a role (developer, system, user, assistant, tool) and content (a string or an array of content parts: {type: text, text}, {type: image_url, image_url: {url, detail}}, {type: input_audio, input_audio: {data, format: wav|mp3}}, {type: file, file: {file_id | file_data, filename}}). Developer messages replace system messages for o1 and newer models.

parameters.name: response_format
parameters.description: Output format: {type: text}; {type: json_schema, json_schema: {name, schema, strict, description}} (Structured Outputs, preferred where supported); or {type: json_object} (older JSON mode, no schema adherence).

parameters.name: max_completion_tokens
parameters.description: Upper bound on generated tokens, including visible output and reasoning tokens.

parameters.name: max_tokens
parameters.description: Deprecated in favor of max_completion_tokens.

parameters.name: temperature
parameters.description: Sampling temperature between 0 and 2.

parameters.name: n
parameters.description: How many choices to generate. Keep n at 1 to minimize cost.

parameters.name: store
parameters.description: Whether to store the output of this chat completion (for model distillation or evals). The reference states no default; the migration guide says chat completions are stored by default for new accounts.

endpoints.title: Create embeddings

endpoints.title: Create transcription
endpoints.description: Transcribes an audio file into text in the input language (multipart form). Files can be up to 25 MB in flac, mp3, mp4, mpeg, mpga, m4a, ogg, wav or webm format. Returns a transcription object whose text field holds the transcript (json, verbose_json or diarized_json formats). It transcribes; it does not summarize.

parameters.name: file
parameters.description: The audio file to transcribe (flac, mp3, mp4, mpeg, mpga, m4a, ogg, wav or webm; up to 25 MB).

parameters.name: model
parameters.description: Transcription model: gpt-transcribe (recommended for recorded speech), gpt-4o-transcribe, gpt-4o-mini-transcribe, gpt-4o-transcribe-diarize (speaker labels; scheduled to shut down 2027-02-26) or whisper-1 (timestamps). The deprecations page schedules whisper-1, gpt-4o-transcribe and gpt-4o-mini-transcribe to shut down on February 26, 2027.

parameters.name: response_format

parameters.name: language
parameters.description: Language hint (ISO-639-1) for models that accept one language hint. For gpt-transcribe the guide says a languages field replaces language; don't send both.

parameters.name: prompt
parameters.description: Unstructured context about the recording (for whisper-1, up to 224 tokens). gpt-4o-transcribe-diarize does not support prompts.

explanation.summary: The embeddings endpoint turns text into vectors (lists of numbers) for similarity and search. Its input accepts an array of strings, so the whole deck goes in one request, and the response's data array holds one embedding per input with an index pointing back to the input's position.
keyIdeas: Match the required OUTPUT type: vectors come from embeddings; text-generation endpoints return words.
Read input limits: an array of up to 2048 strings (and at most 300,000 tokens in total) fits a 200-card deck in one call.
data[].index links each vector to its card; never assume order without checking the documented field.
The model choice is a capability decision, not a ranking: any documented embedding model meets this goal.
